proved_scope: Tagged Analyze versus Complete(model) dispatch: complete returns exactly the control and actual-input data outcomes; analyzer function is irrelevant in that branch.
Complete dispatch invokes no analyzer/default/unresolved lane or body-boundary rule lane. This includes an input for which data outcome is empty.
External call-site report list remains on the common invocation path and is preserved in complete dispatch.
Exact registered method identity selects the model; an equal method spelling with a different identity does not.
Finite registry identity kernel retains registry/caller payloads, rejects other static data and is its own backward identity-filter relation.
Schema metadata does not participate in the abstract semantic outcome key/hash.
Explicit observation-difference witness: complete dispatch preserves cleanup values but omits a baseline body-boundary sink, as newly selected by the user.
not_proved: Production AP schema application/projection, E/mx/layer/protection/primitive/alias behavior, control/exception shape completeness, catalog matching or frontend call-stage integration.
External call-site rule timing, guards/ND bindings, report identity/callback counts or all real predefined models.
A runtime lazy Sequence/iterator implementation or finite query scheduler; valuesFor is a pure actual-input function in this kernel.
Equality of baseline body-boundary observations: the complete branch intentionally skips them.
Demand snapshot/native-record separation or production semantic equality/hashing; those require their own adapters.
Whole-JVM equivalence, runtime implementation or measured savings.
selected_semantic_change: Predefined methods skip their body-boundary rules as explicitly directed; ordinary external call-site rules remain. No event-aware boundary owner is added.

measured_context.limit: Prior campaign only; no measurements for this proposal.
